utterances.text: No, I didn't have any information according to which there was another unit in that area, apart from what I mentioned at the beginning. I said is that there were inhabitants of Gluha Bukovica and Zagradje and they had become part of the 314th Brigade.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But if a unit was engaged in combat or was active in the zone of the responsibility of your battalion, you were informed of the fact?

utterances.speaker: FAHIR CAMDZIC
utterances.text: Well, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Camdzic, in May and June 1993, you were the battalion commander. Did you ever act together or cooperate in combat operations with members of the 7th Muslim Brigade of the 3rd Corps of the BH Army?

utterances.speaker: FAHIR CAMDZIC
utterances.text: No, I never had any contact with units of the 7th.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: During this period, did you ever receive any kind of order according to which you were to take action together with [Realtime transcript read in error "against"] members of the 7th Brigade?

utterances.speaker: FAHIR CAMDZIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let's go back to the 8th of June. In response to a question of my colleague, you said you and part of your battalion - I think you mentioned about 80 men - you said you were in Krpeljici and you were holding the line facing the HVO.

utterances.speaker: FAHIR CAMDZIC
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I think there is an error on page 45 of the transcript, line 5. It says that in response to my question as to whether "the battalion ever acted in combat operations and together with members of the 7th Muslim Brigade", it says "against with the 7th Muslim Brigade." But the witness said he never acted together with members of the 7th Brigade.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, I never acted or took action together with members of the 7th.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You said you were in Krpeljici with about 80 men who were holding the line facing the HVO.

utterances.speaker: FAHIR CAMDZIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: At the beginning of June, we're talking about the 7th and 8th of June, the brigade commander was also in the village of Krpeljici.

utterances.speaker: FAHIR CAMDZIC
utterances.text: Yes, in the village of Krpeljici.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You said in the course of your testimony that the brigade commander during that period when he saw what was happening and saw that the village of Maline had been attacked, the commander forwarded a request to the 1st and the 4th Battalion for assistance.

utterances.speaker: FAHIR CAMDZIC
utterances.text: Yes. That's the 1st and 4th Battalion of the 306th Brigade.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Afterwards, you said that you established contact with the 1st and 4th Battalions when the blockade of that area had been lifted.

utterances.speaker: FAHIR CAMDZIC
utterances.text: That's absolutely correct. When the blockade was lifted, when they reached us, that was when I first established contact with them. Blank page inserted to ensure the pagination between the English and French transcripts correspond

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You then established contact with members of the 1st and 4th Battalions of the 306th?

utterances.speaker: FAHIR CAMDZIC
utterances.text: Well, that's the 1st Battalion because the 4th Battalion was further to the north, but that is where I established contact with the 1st Battalion. Perhaps with parts of the 4th as well. I can't remember exactly, but I'm certain that these men were members of the 306th Brigade.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Of the 1st Battalion?

utterances.speaker: FAHIR CAMDZIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You said that when the brigade commander made this request for assistance for the village of Velika Bukovica, the 1st Battalion came from the village of Mehurici and went in the direction of?

utterances.speaker: FAHIR CAMDZIC
utterances.text: Well, I'm not sure. But they headed in our direction, the village of Krpeljici.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you describe the area.

utterances.speaker: FAHIR CAMDZIC
utterances.text: Well, it's from Mehurici via Simulje, Carine, Radonjici, Krpeljici. That would be the axis.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: On the 8th of June when you finally received information, met on the axis from Mehurici towards Krpeljici, on that date members of the 7th Brigade didn't go into action?

utterances.speaker: FAHIR CAMDZIC
utterances.text: No, I didn't see any members of the 7th there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: According to the information you later received, were any members of the 7th involved in action on that axis?

utterances.speaker: FAHIR CAMDZIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much. We have no further questions, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, and the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. Cross-examined by Mr. Mundis:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Good morning, Witness. My name is Daryl Mundis, and along with my colleagues here this morning, I represent the Prosecution in this case. I want to assure you, sir, that our intention this morning is not in any way to confuse you. We are simply going to ask you some questions, and I would ask that if you find any of my questions confusing or you don't understand the question, if you simply ask me to clarify or repeat the question, and I will do that for you. Do you understand that?

utterances.speaker: FAHIR CAMDZIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, let me start by asking you a few preliminary questions about your experience and background as a graduate of the military academy in Belgrade and a former company commander in the JNA. You told us that at the time you left the JNA, you were a company commander in the infantry. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: FAHIR CAMDZIC
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And moving from that position into the time period when you were with the sector staff in Mehurici and the Mehurici detachment, and finally, the commander of the 2nd Battalion of the 306th Mountain Brigade, would it be fair to say that based on your military experience you had a lot of close contact in dealing with soldiers?

utterances.speaker: FAHIR CAMDZIC
utterances.text: What do you mean, "close contact"? I don't understand. I had contact with the soldiers, but as to close contact I don't understand.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let's start with the company. A company in the JNA has approximately how many men in it? A JNA infantry company.

utterances.speaker: FAHIR CAMDZIC
utterances.text: Well, it would have about 135 men.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And how closely involved would a JNA infantry company commander be with the men that were under his command? How much interaction would you have with them?

utterances.speaker: FAHIR CAMDZIC
utterances.text: Well, it would go through the system of control and command. That's how it operated.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, I understand that. But my question is more like: On a day-to-day basis, how much interaction would you have had or did you have as a company commander with the men who were part of your infantry company when you were in the JNA?

utterances.speaker: FAHIR CAMDZIC
utterances.text: Well, I didn't have contact on a daily basis, apart from the daily activities they had. The platoon commanders had more contact with the soldiers than I did. It depended on what had been planned for the day. But when necessary, if this was part of the plan for the day's activities, I would have contact with the soldiers.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let me focus now on the time period when you were in Mehurici. You told us that you spent a great deal of your time on the Vlasic plateau. And I'm talking about 1992 at this point. You spent a great deal of time on the Vlasic plateau. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: FAHIR CAMDZIC
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That position, was that one in which you had a great deal of contact with the soldiers who were under your command?

utterances.speaker: FAHIR CAMDZIC
utterances.text: Yes. Every day, I spent time with the soldiers at the lines.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, let me talk about the time period or ask you a few questions about the time period when you were the commander of the 2nd Battalion of the 306th Mountain Brigade. I take it from your answers that you were in that position from roughly November 1992 through the autumn of 1993?

utterances.speaker: FAHIR CAMDZIC
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And I believe, sir, you told us that you had at least during some point in that time period approximately 440 men in your battalion. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: FAHIR CAMDZIC
utterances.text: According to the battalion's establishment, there should have been more men. But it wasn't up to full strength. So I had more or less the number that you have mentioned in my battalion.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And during the period that you were the battalion commander, how many interaction did you have with the soldiers who were members of the battalion? Again, were you spending most of your time in the field with the soldiers, most of your time in the command post? Can you just give us a general sense as to the amount of time you spent with the men.

utterances.speaker: FAHIR CAMDZIC
utterances.text: It depended on the situation. The situations were different. I tried to spend as much time as possible with my soldiers. I don't know how long I spent with them, but I'm certain that I spent a lot of time with them.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And can you briefly tell us a little bit about what you envisioned your role being with respect to the soldiers that were in your battalion. What was your job as the commander? What did that entail?

utterances.speaker: FAHIR CAMDZIC
utterances.text: My job as commander of that unit entailed implementing all orders received from my superior. It entailed influencing the soldiers, motivating the soldiers, because these men were not professional men. They were between 18 and 16 [as interpreted] years of age. They weren't professional in the usual sense of the term, so I tried to explain the situation to them, and I tried to explain to them why we had to implement the order.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] On page 50 line 12, I just want to correct something. It says that their age was from between 18 and 60 -- it says from 18 to 16, whereas the witness said from 18 to 60.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let's just clarify that. The soldiers you had in your battalion were between the ages of 18 and 60 years of age.

utterances.speaker: FAHIR CAMDZIC
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I take it, sir, in light of the different types of tasks that you just told us about, including explaining things to them, that part of what you needed to do was to be concerned with their welfare, the well being of the soldiers that were under your command. Would that be a fair characterisation?

utterances.speaker: FAHIR CAMDZIC
utterances.text: I haven't understood the last part of your question. What do you mean when you said that I had to be concerned with something that --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would you be concerned with the welfare and well being of the soldiers who were part of your command? Would that be part of your task as a commander?

utterances.speaker: FAHIR CAMDZIC
utterances.text: Well, naturally. I would be concerned with them. I would be concerned with ensuring that they had enough food, ammunition, et cetera, and I also had to concern myself with their health, et cetera.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let me move on to a slightly different topic, then. You told us Blank page inserted to ensure the pagination between the English and French transcripts correspond in response to some questions right at the end of the examination by Madam Residovic, you were talking about disciplinary measures that were taken against soldiers who were part of the 306th Mountain Brigade. Do you remember telling us about --

utterances.speaker: FAHIR CAMDZIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, can you recall the names of any soldier who was a member of the 2nd Battalion of the 306th Mountain Brigade who was disciplined during the time period you were the battalion commander?

utterances.speaker: FAHIR CAMDZIC
utterances.text: It's very difficult for me to answer that question. I know that disciplinary measures were taken against soldiers, but since I wasn't from that area, I really didn't know the names, family names. So it's very difficult for me to remember the names of the soldiers against whom disciplinary measures were taken. But it's certain that there were such men.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let me move up, then, a step. I assume based on this answer that the same would hold once you moved up to the 306th Battalion as the operations officer. You don't recall the names of any soldiers from any battalions of the 306th Mountain Brigade who were disciplined?

utterances.speaker: FAHIR CAMDZIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you recall, again going back to the time period you were the commander of the 2nd Battalion of the 306th Mountain Brigade, do you recall the types of offences for which any soldiers under your command were disciplined during the time period you were the commander?

utterances.speaker: FAHIR CAMDZIC
utterances.text: Well, they were disciplined mainly for refusing to obey orders. There were also attempts to loot property, and disciplinary measures were taken in relation to such acts. Anything else that didn't concern the military -- or if anything was done that wasn't considered to be appropriate military behaviour, we would take all the measures that we thought were necessary.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let me ask you about -- you mentioned looting property. Do you recall the specifics as to the location where any property was looted that soldiers of the 2nd Battalion of the 306th Mountain Brigade were disciplined?

utterances.speaker: FAHIR CAMDZIC
utterances.text: Well, I know there was looting in the area. As far as I can remember, I don't think members of the 2nd Battalion were involved. But I can't be sure.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you say "in the area," what area are you referring to? The area where the 2nd Battalion was located?

utterances.speaker: FAHIR CAMDZIC
utterances.text: Well, I'm referring to the area covered not just by the 2nd Battalion, but the area in general. In the area covered by the 2nd Battalion, there were places such as Guca Gora, Radojcici, et cetera. Since most people passed through that area, people who weren't soldiers, refugees from various regions, Chetniks, HVO members, well, people tried to get by as best they could. So that's what happened.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let me try to focus our attention. I'm referring specifically to looting carried out by soldiers who were members of the 306th Mountain Brigade. Are you aware of incidents of looting by soldiers of the 306th Mountain Brigade during the time period when you were the commander of the 2nd Battalion of that brigade?

utterances.speaker: FAHIR CAMDZIC
utterances.text: I'm not aware of such incidents. I can only speak for my own battalion at that time. I don't think there was any looting, but the 306th Brigade covered a vast area so I couldn't have known about such incidents, nor was it my responsibility to know about such incidents.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I understand that, sir. Let me just try to clarify the situation then. You were unaware, because it wasn't your responsibility, of any instances where soldiers from any battalions other than your own were disciplined for looting?

utterances.speaker: FAHIR CAMDZIC
utterances.text: No, I wasn't aware of that. It wasn't necessary for me to have such information.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you are not aware of any incidents where soldiers of the 2nd Battalion of the 306th Mountain Brigade were disciplined for looting?

utterances.speaker: FAHIR CAMDZIC
utterances.text: I really can't remember. Perhaps there were such incidents. I can't really say. Disciplinary measures weren't taken, but I didn't have any information indicating that members of the 2nd Battalion had been involved in looting. Because at the time, the 2nd Battalion was engaged at the contact line. So they quite simply didn't have any time to get involved in this. They were facing the Serbian and Montenegrin aggressor, and they were also facing the HVO.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you, sir. Let me move on now to a different topic. You indicated earlier, I think, on two separate occasions this morning, including at page 42, line 8, you said "our units entered Velika Bukovica on the 8th." Let me ask you a few questions about that. First of all, do you remember saying that, and is that the case?

utterances.speaker: FAHIR CAMDZIC
utterances.text: Perhaps I did say on the 8th. It's possible. I don't know. Maybe I said, that but I'm not sure.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you recall approximately when the town of Velika Bukovica was attacked by the HVO?

utterances.speaker: FAHIR CAMDZIC
utterances.text: The HVO attacked Velika Bukovica on the 4th of June 1993.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And approximately how long after that was the response of units of the 306th Mountain Brigade?

utterances.speaker: FAHIR CAMDZIC
utterances.text: I think it was four days later, on the 8th.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And sir, which units of the 306th Mountain Brigade participated in driving the HVO out of the village of Velika Bukovica?

utterances.speaker: FAHIR CAMDZIC
utterances.text: I wouldn't say that they were driven out. In my view, this territory was occupied, and we liberated the area of Velika Bukovica. The 306th Brigade, its 1st and 4th Battalions liberated Velika Bukovica.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So the 2nd Battalion was not involved in the liberation, as you put it, of Velika Bukovica?

utterances.speaker: FAHIR CAMDZIC
utterances.text: No. We didn't stand a chance to do that, although we wanted to do that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Other than the 1st and 4th Battalions of the 306th Mountain Brigade, were you aware of any other units of the ABiH 3rd Corps that participated in liberating the village of Velika Bukovica?

utterances.speaker: FAHIR CAMDZIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let me ask you a few questions now about Guca Gora. You testified earlier today, page 33, line 19, that "we entered Guca Gora" and you then said "we passed through," and this was during the period from the 8th to the 10th of June 1993. Do you recall the precise or the date that your battalion, the 2nd Battalion of the 306th Mountain Brigade, entered Guca Gora?

utterances.speaker: FAHIR CAMDZIC
utterances.text: Yes. I remember well. This was on the 10th of June 1993. And when I said "entered and passed through," this means that we just moved on to get to the contact line with the HVO. There was no conflict in Guca Gora. That's why we didn't stay there any longer. We moved on to establish a line where we would finally stop.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And approximately to the best of your recollection, sir, what time did the 2nd Battalion of the 306th Mountain Brigade enter and pass through Guca Gora on 10 June 1993?

utterances.speaker: FAHIR CAMDZIC
utterances.text: Yes. It was not very early. I believe that we started moving between 8.00 and 9.00 on the 10th of June. And we passed through -- it took us about two hours to get there, so we passed through -- it took us about two hours to get there, so we passed through and reached our lines about half past 11.00. We linked up with the villagers of Radojcici, with the unit that was on the strength of the 2nd Battalion.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, sir, I take it from your answer that you were actually accompanying your battalion as they entered and passed through Guca Gora on the 10th of June 1993?

utterances.speaker: FAHIR CAMDZIC
utterances.text: Yes, I was with my battalion.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And sir, on the morning when you say "we started moving between 0800 and 0900 on the 10th of June 1993," where did you start from?

utterances.speaker: FAHIR CAMDZIC
utterances.text: We started from the area of Krpeljici. The village of Krpeljici borders on Guca Gora, and from the lines where we had stopped on the 8th, we continued. Prior to that, there was a reconnaissance, and we established that there were no members of the HVO or civilians there. Our units that were sent to reconnoiter it, they did the job very well. They established the situation just as it was.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, when you say there was reconnaissance and our units were sent to reconnoiter, can you tell us what units were sent to reconnoiter Guca Gora on the 10th of June 1993?

utterances.speaker: FAHIR CAMDZIC
utterances.text: Those were volunteers, men who volunteered, who were members of the companies in Krpeljici and Maline. It was not a large group. There may have been five to seven men who were locals of the area who knew the area well. It was not a unit. They were just volunteers that I singled out to do the job.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I take it, sir, now that you've mentioned this - I was going to ask you this later but I'll do so now - you told us that the members of the 306th Mountain Brigade were all recruited and replenished from the areas where that battalion operated?

utterances.speaker: FAHIR CAMDZIC
utterances.text: Are you referring to the battalion or the entire 306th Brigade?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: No, I'm referring, sir, to the 2nd Battalion of the 306th Mountain Brigade. It was recruited and replenished from men who were from the area, and you gave us the villages earlier, where that battalion primarily operated. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: FAHIR CAMDZIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I take it, sir, there were certain advantages in having local men in the sense they knew the terrain, they knew routes, they knew pathways through the forests and mountains, et cetera. Would that be fair to say?

utterances.speaker: FAHIR CAMDZIC
utterances.text: It would be fair to say that if -- that we were not blocked, that we were engaged and deployed around these villages, and we were defending ourselves. So this did not have any special impact. It was not to our advantage to have locals as members of our unit, locals who were familiar with routes and pathways and so on and so forth.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Mr. President, with the assistance of the usher, I would ask that some maps be produced for the witness, and I would ask him to make some markings on the maps. We do have sufficient copies for everyone in the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, I'd ask you to take a look at the map which is on the projector to your right and ask you to -- let me ask you first if you recognise the locations that are shown on this map.

utterances.speaker: FAHIR CAMDZIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And first, sir, if you could take the pointer, the metal pointer that's right by your left arm, I'd ask you to point to Krpeljici. And if it's possible, to further identify where the command post of the 2nd Battalion of the 306th Mountain Brigade was located at the time you were the commander.

utterances.speaker: FAHIR CAMDZIC
utterances.text: This is Krpeljici. This is the village of Krpeljici. The command of -- the command post of my battalion was here. This is the local commune -- community building or hall.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, if the usher could provide you with a fine-point marker, I would ask you to circle the location where your command post was located on the map, please.

utterances.speaker: FAHIR CAMDZIC
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And if you could perhaps just right above that write "2/306."

utterances.speaker: FAHIR CAMDZIC
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, sir, again with the silver pointer rather than the marker, I would ask you to point to, if you see it on the map, the monastery in Guca Gora.

utterances.speaker: FAHIR CAMDZIC
utterances.text: [Indicates]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you please take the marker and circle the monastery.

utterances.speaker: FAHIR CAMDZIC
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, sir, again with the silver pointer, I would ask you to the best of your recollection if you can trace the route that the 2nd Battalion of the 306th Mountain Brigade took on the 10th of June 1993 as you entered and passed through Guca Gora.

utterances.speaker: FAHIR CAMDZIC
utterances.text: We started from here, and this is how we moved. The axis of our movement was along the road towards the village of Hraban [phoen]. This was the route.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, you indicated an area and you said "we started from here." What was the location you started from?

utterances.speaker: FAHIR CAMDZIC
utterances.text: This was the line that we reached on the 8th. And we were stopped there, we were there until the 10th of June. We were providing security for Krpeljici, and at the same time we were getting ready to move on.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So the area that you've just indicated was, in effect, a line? There was a line there. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: FAHIR CAMDZIC
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct. That's the line that we reached on the 8th of June.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And on the 10th, as your unit was preparing to move through Guca Gora, you -- your forces, that is, the 2nd Battalion of the 306th Mountain Brigade, gathered at the front line, then. Would that be correct?

utterances.speaker: FAHIR CAMDZIC
utterances.text: It was already on the line. That battalion was already holding that line. According to our very precise information, there was nobody in Guca Gora. We made sure that there were no booby traps, as a normal precaution measure. So we set off, and we moved through Guca Gora without any problems.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, was the second battalion of the 306th Mountain Brigade the first unit of the 3rd Corps to enter Guca Gora on the 10th of June 1993?

utterances.speaker: FAHIR CAMDZIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes. That's the unit which entered.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: During the time, sir, that your unit entered and passed through Guca Gora, did you see any other units of the 3rd Corps on the 10th of June 1993 in Guca Gora?

utterances.speaker: FAHIR CAMDZIC
utterances.text: No. On that day, I didn't see any other unit except for the unit of the 306th, which was there -- the battalion that I was a member of as well.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And sir, when you say "the battalion that I was a member of," you're talking about the 2nd Battalion of the 306th Mountain Brigade, and in fact --

utterances.speaker: FAHIR CAMDZIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: -- and in fact you were the commander of that unit on the 10th of June?

utterances.speaker: FAHIR CAMDZIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, I would now ask with the black marker if you could please draw the path or the route that the 2nd Battalion of the 306th Mountain Brigade took on the 10th of June from that front line through Guca Gora to the point where you eventually stopped on the 10th of June.

utterances.speaker: FAHIR CAMDZIC
utterances.text: [Marks] We stopped around here, very close to Radojcici.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And sir, approximately how long did it take you to get to that point that you stopped -- where you stopped?

utterances.speaker: FAHIR CAMDZIC
utterances.text: I've already said that. It didn't take long. Some two hours, two and a half hours. Not more than that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, during the day of the 8th of June 1993, as you left the front line at Krpeljici to this new front line that was established, were the members of your battalion on foot, or did you have any type of motorised transport? I'm sorry, that should be the 10th of June, I'm sorry. On the 10th of June, did your unit move on foot, or did you have any type of motorised transport?

utterances.speaker: FAHIR CAMDZIC
utterances.text: We moved on foot, of course.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And again, just so we're clear, sir, how many soldiers of the 2nd Battalion, 306th Mountain Brigade, passed through Guca Gora on that day? How many soldiers were with you on that day, the 10th of June 1993?

utterances.speaker: FAHIR CAMDZIC
utterances.text: These were mostly men who were engaged at the time when Krpeljici was encircled. There couldn't have been more than 50 of us among those who entered and reached those lines.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you, Witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Mr. President, the next thing the Prosecution would respectfully request to do is to show the witness an excerpt from one of the videotapes which is currently in evidence. I note the time, however, and we probably can't get through that and ask those questions prior to the break. So with all due respect, we would ask that the break be taken a little bit early. We can then, of course, resume a little bit earlier than usual, and we'll move on to that videotape.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well, then. It is 20 past 12.00. We are going to make a break until quarter to 1.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We resume.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. Before I show the witness a video, I did have a couple of follow-up questions.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, on the -- during the first two weeks in June 1993, was the 306 Mountain Brigade part of the operation group Bosanska Krajina?

utterances.speaker: FAHIR CAMDZIC
utterances.text: You are asking me something that I don't know. I was not a member of the command of the 306th. In my view, it wasn't, but I don't know. I wouldn't know. I was the commander of a battalion, and I received orders from my brigade commander.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Fair enough, sir. But let me just ask you this, then, or to clarify this: You're not aware of who your brigade commander reported to?

utterances.speaker: FAHIR CAMDZIC
utterances.text: No. There was no need for me to know that. I had my commander, and that's it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But sir, you told us earlier, I believe, that at some point after the 10th of June 1993, your battalion moved towards the direction of Radojcici. Is that correct? Or did I misunderstand what you just told us?

utterances.speaker: FAHIR CAMDZIC
utterances.text: After having stopped, we just continued moving along the line that I pointed to you. There was no obstacles for us towards Radojcici. And when we got there, we reached this line which was never moved, either forward or backward. We arrived in that village where members of my battalion were.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay, sir, I'd ask you, sir, again just before we go to the videotape, if you could again turn to the map that you've marked and which is to your right, and with the pointer, if you could again point to the place where you've marked that the 2nd Battalion of the 306th Mountain Brigade stopped on the 10th of June 1993 at about 11.30 in the morning.

utterances.speaker: FAHIR CAMDZIC
utterances.text: [Indicates]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, how long, then, for purposes of clarification, how long did the 2nd Battalion remain at that location?

utterances.speaker: FAHIR CAMDZIC
utterances.text: It stayed there for a very short time, maybe an hour or so. We proceeded very soon. This complete area was free. We continued towards Radojcici. We arrived at the line here, and we stayed here at the very end until the moment we were linked up with our members. So our stop was very brief. This area was completely empty, and we just moved on.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If you could, then, please, sir, take the black marker once again, thin black marker, and continue the line indicating where the 2nd Battalion of the 306th Mountain Brigade went on the 10th of June 1993.

utterances.speaker: FAHIR CAMDZIC
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And for the record, it would appear that the witness has marked what appears to be an arrowhead to the right of the word "Radojcici" on the map.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, at that point where the arrowhead touches the horizontal line, is that where the 2nd Battalion of the 306th Mountain Brigade stopped on the 10th of June 1993?

utterances.speaker: FAHIR CAMDZIC
utterances.text: Not only there. Parallel with this, with the movement of these units I had as well. But since you were interested in this axis, this is where I stopped, and this includes this very place. And along the front line. And maybe I moved a bit further, but I didn't go this way. This was not me.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you, Witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Mr. President, I would now ask that the witness be shown a clip of P482, which is a videotape. And for the record, this videotape contains two parts. We will be showing the time period 1 minute -- excuse me, 1 hour, 8 minutes, 34 seconds through 1 hour, 11 minutes, 22 seconds on part 1 of P482. I would propose that the witness be shown this without the audio, simply look at the video, and I'll then ask him some questions. But I do see my learned colleague on her feet, so I will defer to her.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, I would like my friend to clarify his reasons for showing this videoclip to the witness since this witness has not testified to anything that is contained in this videoclip.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Mundis.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I apologise. One more thing: I would kindly ask my learned friend to first give us the reasons, and then if the Prosecutor could first show us the clip without the sound, and after that if the witness could be presented everything, that none of the elements should be presented to the witness before the videoclip is shown to him and before the questions are put to him.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] There is a solution that may be consistent with what the Defence counsel has requested. Can the witness be taken out of the courtroom, please. Mr. Mundis, we're listening.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. This clip, which is about 2 minutes and 45 seconds long shows the monastery in Guca Gora. It is in evidence obviously as Prosecution Exhibit 482. We would propose proceeding in the same manner that we have proceeded with respect to other clips that have been shown to Defence witnesses; that is, we will play without the audio. As I indicated to Mr. Bourgon at the break, there is some Arabic script, and on the top of the video in English, it says "operation Guca Gora." We would propose that the audio be turned down, that the witness be asked to watch the clip, which again is 2 minutes and 45 seconds long, watch it in its entirety. Then I would ask the witness to perhaps again watch it and to tell us what, if anything, he sees or recognises on the videotape. Among the questions we would be asking would be, if the witness is able to answer, the location where the videotape was shot; in other words, what the vantage point, and perhaps he can mark on the map where he believes the person taking the video was standing at the time the video was taken. It does show what appears to be combatants of some type. Perhaps the witness can comment on that. And we would simply ask him for any comments or observations he could make with respect to the videotape. I'm certainly not going to tell him when the video was taken or anything like that. I'm certainly not going to be testifying. The tape is in evidence. We would simply ask that he be shown it and ask him to make some comments or observations and then ask him a very few specific questions about where, if he knows, the location of the video or the videographer was standing at the time the videotape was made.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Defence.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, the fact that the Guca Gora monastery can be recognised on the tape is certainly something that could not be tied with this witness because the Prosecutor has already had witnesses that could testify to that. However, as for the other issues that were raised by my learned friend, maybe it would be good if the -- my learned friend first put questions to the witness, the questions that he has just mentioned, whether he knew that there was somebody recording, whether there were any other men in front of the monastery and so on and so forth. And only after that, maybe my learned friend should show the videoclip to the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The Defence suggests that the Prosecution should ask some preliminary questions in order to find out whether the -- there were any other men on the spot. What do you think of that, Mr. Mundis? It may be relevant because the witness has said that there were some other men in Guca Gora on that morning. There were some 50 other men there on the 10th of June. And Defence suggests and would like you to put some preliminary questions. What is your view on that?

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: I appreciate the suggestions of my learned colleague. Of course, Mr. President, the Prosecution would take the position that the way we conduct our cross-examination is -- as long as it's consistent with the Rules and the orders of the Trial Chamber, that's up to us as to how we wish to proceed. Again, we could ask some questions about the -- of the witness, and then show him the tape, and he might not recognise anything that's on the tape. It would seem to us the best way to proceed would be to simply show him the tape, and then ask him to make any comments about what's contained on the tape. It's entirely possible that what's shown on the tape was not in the witness's view taken on the day in question. It could be taken from a completely different angle than the witness has testified about how he entered Guca Gora, et cetera. So it seems to us the better way, since the tape is in evidence, is to show him the tape and then ask him the questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. The Trial Chamber has decided how to proceed. The Prosecution will first show the witness the video and will then put questions to him. Could we have the witness back in the courtroom, please.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, we're going to show you now a videotape which the usher will assist you so that you can see it on the screen in front of you. Before we do that, I simply want to inform you of the procedure that we will be working with this afternoon. I'm going to show you this clip. It runs a little bit less than 3 minutes. There will be no sound. I simply, first of all, want you first of all to look at the videotape. Then I will ask you a few questions about the tape, and perhaps we will show the tape again, and if you can -- if there's anything on the tape that you recognise or you wish to tell us about, you can then on the second time we watch the videotape tell us to stop and describe what you see on the videotape in front of you. Do you understand this procedure?

utterances.speaker: FAHIR CAMDZIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Mr. President, with your leave, I ask that the tape be shown now, please. Mr. President, we seem to be having a technical problem. Perhaps we can have a technician assist us in the...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Registrar, could you call the technician, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: It seems possible, Mr. President, to observe it on the "computer evidence" channel, if that would be acceptable. But I'm not sure if that's being broadcast outside of the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, let me ask you first of all if you recognised anything that you saw in the videoclip that you just watched.

utterances.speaker: FAHIR CAMDZIC
utterances.text: No. I recognised the church. That's what I recognised. But nothing else.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And when you say "church," sir, can you be more specific in terms of what it was that you saw?

utterances.speaker: FAHIR CAMDZIC
utterances.text: Well, I saw the church in Guca Gora. I saw these members. That's all I know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you recognise any of the combatants that were shown on the videotape? Or can you tell us anything about any of the people that you saw on the videotape?

utterances.speaker: FAHIR CAMDZIC
utterances.text: No, I couldn't say anything. I didn't see them, and at the time that I passed through they certainly were not there. I don't know when this was shot, but there's nothing I can say about this.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let me just ask you one last question about what we just saw on the videotape, sir. Do you know -- or based on being in the area in June of 1993, do you have any idea in the opening shots of the video, the first shot that shows the monastery in Guca Gora, do you have any idea where the person taking that picture might have been standing?

utterances.speaker: FAHIR CAMDZIC
utterances.text: Well, no. I don't have any idea. I don't know where it could have been shot from.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you don't know which angle or which direction the photographer was standing in, in relation to the monastery?

utterances.speaker: FAHIR CAMDZIC
utterances.text: No, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, sir, when you -- when the 2nd Battalion of the 306th Mountain Brigade passed through Guca Gora, did you leave any soldiers from your battalion behind in the village of Guca Gora?

utterances.speaker: FAHIR CAMDZIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So to the best of your recollection, none of your soldiers were left behind to guard or to protect the property in Guca Gora, having -- your battalion having passed through?

utterances.speaker: FAHIR CAMDZIC
utterances.text: That's what I said at the beginning. I had received an order from the brigade commander to provide security for this building. And I carried out the order. Perhaps two or three soldiers stayed down there with the civilian protection who were there with us. But I really don't know what happened because I was involved in the operations I have already referred to, both on the left and on the right side.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, do you have any recollection as to how long the two or three soldiers that stayed there remained in Guca Gora?

utterances.speaker: FAHIR CAMDZIC
utterances.text: I can't remember how long they stayed there. I don't have any information about that because I was elsewhere all the time, and I was linking up the lines which I went to with the combatants.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay, sir. I'd like to draw your attention back to what we have referred to as Prosecution Exhibit P619.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Mr. President, as we did with the previous witness, we were able to get the best copy that the Tribunal has out of the evidence unit, and I would ask that the witness be shown this copy of this document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] P699? I see Mr. Bourgon on his feet.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: 690. I misspoke. 690.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, in response to some questions from the Defence, I believe you told us that you had never seen this document before. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: FAHIR CAMDZIC
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'd ask you to turn to the third page of this document at the bottom on the left-hand side where it's indicated to whom this order is addressed. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: FAHIR CAMDZIC
utterances.text: I can see it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you see that the document is addressed to the commander of the 2nd Battalion of the 306th Mountain Brigade?

utterances.speaker: FAHIR CAMDZIC
utterances.text: It probably should have been addressed to him.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Bourgon.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President. I'd like to know if the witness has the original that my colleague showed me during the break, or does he have the same document that we have, which is illegible?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Mundis, does the witness have the original document?

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Yes, he does, Mr. President. As I said, it's the boast copy that the Tribunal has. I don't know if it's the actual original --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We could put it on the ELMO in that case so that everyone can see it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, again, Witness, I draw your attention to the number 5 under the list of addressees. It does, in fact, say commander, 2nd Battalion, 306th Mountain Brigade. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: FAHIR CAMDZIC
utterances.text: That's what it says.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But again, you don't recall ever having received this document?

utterances.speaker: FAHIR CAMDZIC
utterances.text: No. I can see that it says "to the commander of the MOS company." That's my company. That's what I said in response to the Defence counsel. But there's no logic here. Why should the brigade command assign a task to my company, to my subordinate unit.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, do you recognise the signature that's on this document?

utterances.speaker: FAHIR CAMDZIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is that, in fact, Esad Sipic's signature?

utterances.speaker: FAHIR CAMDZIC
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: That document can be retrieved from the ELMO.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, I have just a few more questions, and I believe we will finish in the next few moments. I want to ask you now -- I want to turn your attention to the persons that you described as the Arabs who later became known as the mujahedin. Now, did you ever hear of any instance where these mujahedin or Arabs in Mehurici were recruiting any soldiers from the Travnik municipal Territorial Defence staff or any of its lower level units?

utterances.speaker: FAHIR CAMDZIC
utterances.text: No, they never recruited in that area. They only obtained followers there. They obtained followers who were poor, who didn't have anything to eat. So they would give them food aid, and that's how they gained these followers. And as they had money, this is also probably a way in which they found supporters, followers.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But to the best of your recollection, then, none of these poor people that they recruited were members of the Territorial Defence staff? Any component unit of the Territorial Defence staff. Is that right? As far as you know?

utterances.speaker: FAHIR CAMDZIC
utterances.text: I didn't say that there were no such members. There were such cases. We had quite a few problems, as I said, for this very reason, because this is how members of those detachments went to join them, on their own initiative, as I have already said. But it was very difficult for us, for us to replenish and recruit. So the situation was quite difficult.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did the same situation occur after the formation of the brigades? That is, did soldiers leave the brigades to go be with the mujahedin?

utterances.speaker: FAHIR CAMDZIC
utterances.text: Well, there were probably such cases, too. As far as my battalion is concerned, I can say that there were not many such cases. There were a few who left, but there were probably others from other units who left in this way. I don't know exactly.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, do you know whether the mujahedin trained and/or equipped these people who joined them?

utterances.speaker: FAHIR CAMDZIC
utterances.text: I don't know. But as far as I know, there was religious training. There wasn't much military training. And in return, they would give them uniforms. They would be happy to be given a rifle, et cetera. And these rifles would be obtained on the black market, for example.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And the mujahedin would obtain rifles on the black market and provide them to these young men?

utterances.speaker: FAHIR CAMDZIC
utterances.text: As I said, there were some lucky individuals. They didn't give these things to everyone. Not everyone would receive weapons from them. Perhaps they liked certain individuals, and then gave them the weapons.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did any of these soldiers from your battalion who you've told us left - you said there were a few - did any of them ever return to the battalion after receiving uniforms or weapons from the mujahedin?

utterances.speaker: FAHIR CAMDZIC
utterances.text: No. There were very few of them. Five or six of them, I think. But they never returned. I carried out a replenishment of a certain kind. They left. And in my opinion, they were deserters.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, sir, you told us at page 16, line 20 earlier this morning that "we didn't feel safe with these foreigners so close to us." And I believe that was in the context of the time period of the late summer, early fall of 1992. Is that correct? Is that a fair statement of your testimony?

utterances.speaker: FAHIR CAMDZIC
utterances.text: Well, it's fair in the sense that I and the command had to be secure. I had to be alone. They arrived, and I didn't feel comfortable in their presence.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Why is that, sir?

utterances.speaker: FAHIR CAMDZIC
utterances.text: Well, quite simply because I didn't know who these people were. I didn't know where they had come from. I didn't know why they were there. It was said that they were representatives of humanitarian organisations, but without checking up on this, it was difficult for me to know why they were there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You also told us that you told or expressed your concerns to your commander who at the time was Haso Ribo. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: FAHIR CAMDZIC
utterances.text: Yes, that's what I said.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you recall if you raised these concerns with him on one occasion or more than one occasion?

utterances.speaker: FAHIR CAMDZIC
utterances.text: Well, whenever we spoke freely to each other, I drew his attention to the fact. It wasn't as if we were that concerned, but they had started finding followers, local soldiers in the units, and I was afraid there might be a conflict of some kind because there were people who supported them and people who were against them in that area.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you recall the reaction, if any, of Mr. Ribo when you informed him of your concerns?

utterances.speaker: FAHIR CAMDZIC
utterances.text: Well, he probably reacted. I don't know for sure. All I know is that I received instructions according to which I was to wait. I was told that it would be resolved at some level. And while I was waiting for a response, I left the Mehurici area, so I don't know.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Bourgon.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President. I think that something is missing from the transcript. Page 74, line 8, as far as I know, according to what I heard in French, the witness said that there were people who were against them in the sector and who were afraid that this might turn into a conflict. The last part of the sentence does not appear in the transcript. Perhaps the witness could confirm that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Mr. Mundis. Could you ask the witness to specify that aspect.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, you told us that there were some people who supported them, referring to the mujahedin, and some people who were against them in that area. Was there concern about a conflict opening up with the mujahedin?

utterances.speaker: FAHIR CAMDZIC
utterances.text: Well, I wasn't that much afraid of a conflict with mujahedin; I was more afraid of a conflict with our inhabitants who had joined them.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, when you say "I wasn't that much afraid of a conflict with the mujahedin," can you tell us why? Why you weren't afraid of a conflict with the mujahedin?

utterances.speaker: FAHIR CAMDZIC
utterances.text: Well, I wasn't afraid for a number of reasons. Firstly, they were there as humanitarian workers. Secondly, there were fewer of them than us. So I'm sure they wouldn't have planned to do anything there. There weren't that many of them. I never saw more than about 20 of them, or 25 of them at the most, in a group in that area. So there were very few of them.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So I take it from that answer, sir, that from a military point of view, they didn't pose any threat to your unit or the units that were in the area of Mehurici?

utterances.speaker: FAHIR CAMDZIC
utterances.text: No, they didn't pose a threat to anyone there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, you also told us, page 18, line 2, that - and this is in the context of when you were discussing the issue of the mujahedin with the war presidency - you said "the mujahedin probably didn't trust me." Do you remember saying that?

utterances.speaker: FAHIR CAMDZIC
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What made you say that, sir? What would be the basis for the mujahedin being distrustful of you?

utterances.speaker: FAHIR CAMDZIC
utterances.text: Well, I was a member of the JNA. We knew what the JNA did in that territory. And since that is my background, they did not trust me.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'm afraid, sir, I don't quite understand. When you say "we knew what the JNA did in that territory. And since that is my background, they did not trust me," can you perhaps explain or elaborate a little bit on what you mean?

utterances.speaker: FAHIR CAMDZIC
utterances.text: Well, in the territory of the former Yugoslavia, we know that there was a conflict in Slovenia. We know that there was a conflict in Croatia. We know that the JNA was involved in all of this. We know the JNA members were involved in this. So I came from the same sort of background. And they went from one fallout to another and attacked one place at a time, so they didn't trust me very much because up until the 1st of April, I was with them.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did the mujahedin that were in the school in Mehurici know that you had formerly been with the JNA?

utterances.speaker: FAHIR CAMDZIC
utterances.text: I don't know, but I assumed that they did. I can't be certain. I never spoke to them.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Let me ask you this, then: During the time period when you were with the Territorial Defence sector staff in Mehurici, you told us that you spent a great deal of time on the Vlasic plateau and on Mount Vlasic. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: FAHIR CAMDZIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And during this time period in 1992, you were primarily engaged against, as you call them, the Serbian and Montenegrin aggressors. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: FAHIR CAMDZIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: At any time while you were operating on the Vlasic plateau or on Mount Vlasic, did you see any of these mujahedin on Vlasic plateau or Mount Vlasic?

utterances.speaker: FAHIR CAMDZIC
utterances.text: No, I didn't. I never saw them while I was up there.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, on page 76, line 13, the words "I was with them," the witness said that he was with the JNA. "With them," we don't know what "them" means. So could this either be clarified -- could the witness say who he was with up until the 1st of April 1992, or could we establish that the witness said that he was in the JNA.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: We can certainly do that. I think it's clear from the context of the answer.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But sir, when you made reference to the mujahedin not trusting you, you were referring to the fact that you had formerly been in the JNA.

utterances.speaker: FAHIR CAMDZIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you believe that perhaps was the grounds for the mujahedin being distrustful of you, as a former member of the JNA.

utterances.speaker: FAHIR CAMDZIC
utterances.text: Not only the mujahedin. I don't know. Others as well. I didn't have anything to do with the mujahedin. They were there. They -- I don't know. That was that, to put it simply.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you, sir. I would ask, if you could please take again the black marker and in the bottom right-hand corner of the map, if you could please sign your name and put today's date, which is 16 November 2004.

utterances.speaker: FAHIR CAMDZIC
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Thank you, sir. Mr. President, the Prosecution has no further questions at this time for this witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The Defence, any re-examination? Re-examined by Ms. Residovic:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Camdzic, my learned friend has asked you several questions about the mujahedin and their relationship with you. When did you leave the elementary school to assume the new duty of the commander of the 1st Battalion [as interpreted]?

utterances.speaker: FAHIR CAMDZIC
utterances.text: I left the school at the beginning of December 1992, and I became the commander of the 2nd Battalion.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: As you've testified earlier, your command post was in Krpeljici. After that time, did you have any other occasion to go to the primary school in Mehurici or to meet with the mujahedin in any other way?

utterances.speaker: FAHIR CAMDZIC
utterances.text: No. Once I left Mehurici, I never returned to the Mehurici primary school, and I didn't have any contact with the mujahedin after that time.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would I be right to say that whatever you said in response to those questions by my learned friend is relative to the period when you were the commander of the detachment?

utterances.speaker: FAHIR CAMDZIC
utterances.text: Yes, absolutely.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: My learned friend also asked you about the reaction of your superior commander. You have already told me that the sector staff or detachment could not determine who would be accommodated in the primary school. The commander of the municipal staff of the Territorial Defence, did he have the authority to say who should be allowed to go into the school and who shouldn't?

utterances.speaker: FAHIR CAMDZIC
utterances.text: No, I don't think so. I don't think that he had any authorities over that because the civilian structures functioned normally. The situation was somewhat aggravated, but the civilian authorities did function.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You also testified about the departure of these mujahedin from the primary school when the Siprage Battalion was billeted there. Did the Siprage Battalion have any other name? Was it a battalion of the 306th Brigade?

utterances.speaker: FAHIR CAMDZIC
utterances.text: Yes, it was a battalion of the 306th Brigade, and as far as I know it, did not have any other insignia or name. The only marking it had was number one, which stood for the 1st Battalion of the 306th Brigade.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So the so-called Siprage Battalion or the 1st Battalion remained in the school?

utterances.speaker: FAHIR CAMDZIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: There were no two battalions there?

utterances.speaker: FAHIR CAMDZIC
utterances.text: No. There were not.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: My learned friend asked you about some measures that were taken, and you said that you can't remember the names of the persons who these disciplinary measures were taken against. Are you sure that during that period measures were taken against members of the 306th Brigade?

utterances.speaker: FAHIR CAMDZIC
utterances.text: Yes, I'm absolutely sure.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In response to my learned friend's question, you explained that you do not hail from the area, and that you spent only a very short period of time there. In light of that fact, do you know how many disciplinary measures were taken in other battalions? Or maybe at this moment you can't tell us anything about that.

utterances.speaker: FAHIR CAMDZIC
utterances.text: As far as other battalions are concerned, I don't know anything. I have no knowledge of what was being done there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When we're talking about this period of time, can you recall whether there were any cases, and if there were, how many, that such crimes, for example, plunder and other destruction, were perpetrated by civilians rather than army members?

utterances.speaker: FAHIR CAMDZIC
utterances.text: I can say with certainty that most of these crimes were perpetrated by civilians.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who was duty-bound to carry out investigations about crimes perpetrated by civilians?

utterances.speaker: FAHIR CAMDZIC
utterances.text: It was the Ministry of the Interior, the MUP or the SUP, as it was called at the time, that was supposed to carry out the investigations into those crimes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Are you aware how many police stations existed in the territory covered by the 306th Brigade at the time?

utterances.speaker: FAHIR CAMDZIC
utterances.text: I can't be sure about their exact number. I know that there were some. There was a police station in Travnik which had its so-called forward post. I know that in Guca Gora, there was a police station at the beginning. It was in the area of Mosur, and then they were moved to the area of Guca Gora. And I know for sure that there was a police station in Han Bila, and there was one in Mehurici. I don't know whether there were any other police stations in the area.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In response to my learned friend's question, you said that you didn't remember the names of any of the soldiers that allegedly committed crimes against him, the 306th Brigade initiated disciplinary measure. My question to you is as follows: In view of what you did at the time as the commander and what you could learn as a member of the command, are you aware of any of such measures being taken for disciplinary offences that were perpetrated as well as for other actions that were perpetrated?

utterances.speaker: FAHIR CAMDZIC
utterances.text: I know that a lot of disciplinary measures were carried out. A lot of soldiers were remanded in custody. That was when I was the battalion commander. I don't know what was going on in the brigade, at the level of the brigade command. However, I believe that they also instituted measures against their members and that there was a system for that in place.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you were the brigade -- battalion commander and when you worked in the training centre, did you have any problem when you wanted to send men to the lines? Because some of the soldiers had been remanded in custody.

utterances.speaker: FAHIR CAMDZIC
utterances.text: Did you say battalion commander or the brigade commander?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I did say brigade commander. I meant battalion commander. I'm tired.

utterances.speaker: FAHIR CAMDZIC
utterances.text: Yes, I did have problems with sending men to the front lines because some of the men were -- had been remanded this custody, and I would always ask why they were in custody and for how long.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You are a young man. But still, you don't remember some of the names, and you explained how come you don't remember them. Can you tell me how well do you still remember the names of the members of the 306th Brigade? How many of them would you be able to remember?

utterances.speaker: FAHIR CAMDZIC
utterances.text: I really don't know. I don't know how many names I would recall. Maybe up to 50. I wouldn't be able to recall more than 50, I'm sure.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I would also like to know whether you received from your commander an order to put in place all the measures in order to prevent plunder and destruction.

utterances.speaker: FAHIR CAMDZIC
utterances.text: When I was supposed to enter certain places, we would receive very specific orders from the brigade commander. Those orders were either verbal or written.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Earlier today, Mr. Camdzic, you said you are a major in the BiH Army. When you look back and when you remember the times when you were fighting and when you were defending your country, when you were taking certain measures, can you tell the Trial Chamber, do you believe that you did everything that was feasible under the conditions in order to prevent crimes from taking place and in order to discover who the perpetrators of the possible crimes were? What can you tell us about that?

utterances.speaker: FAHIR CAMDZIC
utterances.text: My opinion is that throughout all this time that I spent in the units of the BiH Army, I did everything possible to prevent any unfortunate incidents that may have happened. How successful I was in that, I don't know. But in any case, that was my main objective throughout all this time. I endeavoured to prevent any possible crime.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Camdzic, could you do more? But you didn't because you didn't want to do it or you delayed action until some other time?

utterances.speaker: FAHIR CAMDZIC
utterances.text: I did everything I could. I did not delay any action. I did everything to the best of my ability.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much. I have no further questions.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President. We don't have any re-examination for this witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. It is quarter to 2.00. Your testimony is finished. We would like to thank you for having come to The Hague to testify. We wish you a happy journey back home. I'm going to ask the usher to accompany you out of the courtroom. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I suppose that the Prosecution would like to tender the map into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Yes, we would, Mr. President. And also, if Your Honours would like us to -- perhaps once that's done, we would be in a position to respond at this point to the Defence request for an extension of time with respect to their exhibit and witness list. And I can do that orally in about 3 minutes maximum if you would like us to do that after we've dealt with the map.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] About the map.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No objection, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No objection, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Registrar, a number for the map.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This map will be P937.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. Registrar. This is your Exhibit 690. Mr. Mundis, you have a few minutes to take the floor.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. I did discuss the issue with Mr. Bourgon at the last break. As I think the Chamber is aware, the Prosecution team in this case is a bit challenged when it comes to the French language. He did explain to us the nature of their motion and what it contained. The Prosecution would have no objection to the Defence being entitled to additional time to file their witness and Defence list. I did make our position clear, however, with respect to one issue: The Prosecution is more concerned about the Defence dropping a witness or witnesses than they would be in the case of adding witnesses for the simply reason that quite frequently, as Your Honours can appreciate, we might have a choice of one or two or three witnesses whom we might want to cross-examine on a particular issue, and we might identify one of the later witnesses as being the best witness to present with a certain issue, and so I explained that also to Mr. Bourgon, and I think he has alleviated our concerns with respect to that. But we would have no objection to them being allowed additional time pursuant to the motion that they have filed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We are going to discuss this and tomorrow morning at 9.00 we are going to tell you what we have decided. For tomorrow, we have a witness, so there's no problem. The Witness Number 59. The Judges could not ask this witness any questions. Tomorrow, if you take an hour and a half, that will leave us some time for the questions. If you take more time, this will block us. So again, I would like to ask both parties to try and stick to the time allocated to them in order to allow the Judges to put questions to the witness. Thank you very much, and I invite you to come back tomorrow for a session that starts at 9.00 in the morning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Wednesday, the 17th day of November, 2004, at 9.00 a.m.
